filing_type: Regulation 33 Reviewed Standalone & Consolidated Financial Results
FilingSource: BSE / NSE Corporate Filings & SBI Central Board Analyst Presentation (Q1 FY27)

headline_metrics.pat_yoy_note: Highest-ever quarterly Net Profit driven by benign credit costs (0.38%) and strong treasury/fee income

segment_performance.segment: Retail Personal Banking (Home, Auto & Xpress Credit)
segment_performance.highlight: Home loan book grew +14.2% YoY with industry-lowest Gross NPA of 0.68% in retail mortgages.
Strong working capital and infrastructure loan demand (+16.1% YoY); corporate recoveries exceeded fresh slippages.
Lower sovereign bond yields generated strong mark-to-market (MTM) treasury gains during Q1 FY27.
Digital SME underwriting via YONO Business propelled SME advances past ₹4.6 Lakh Cr (+18.4% YoY).

simple_pointers: **Record Quarterly Net Profit (PAT):** SBI delivered its highest-ever quarterly Net Profit of **₹24,113 Cr** in Q1 FY27, surging **+22.76% QoQ** (vs ₹19,643 Cr in Q4 FY26) and **+13.73% YoY** (vs ₹21,201 Cr in Q1 FY26).

**Resilient Net Interest Income (NII) & Margins:** Net Interest Income stood at **₹41,125 Cr** with Domestic Net Interest Margin (NIM) holding steady at **3.35%**, while total interest revenue reached **₹97,814 Cr** (+10.24% YoY).

**Decade-Best Asset Quality (Low Bad Loans):** Gross Non-Performing Assets (GNPA) improved by 55 bps YoY to **2.21%**, and Net NPA dropped to just **0.57%** with a **91.8% Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR)**.

**Healthy Loan Book & Deposit Franchise:** Total advances expanded **+15.4% YoY** (led by Retail Home Loans and SME credit), backed by India's largest low-cost deposit franchise (**40.7% CASA ratio**).

**Attractive Valuation vs Historical Peers:** Trading at **~10.2x trailing P/E** with Return on Equity (ROE) exceeding **19.4%** and Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) at **14.28%** (57.23% Government of India sovereign ownership).

strengths: Record quarterly Net Profit of ₹24,113 Cr (+22.76% QoQ, +13.73% YoY) with Return on Equity (ROE) above 19%.
Pristine asset quality: Gross NPA down to 2.21%, Net NPA at 0.57%, and 91.8% Provision Coverage Ratio (with AUCA).
Unmatched deposit franchise (40.7% CASA ratio) and 57.23% sovereign backing by the Government of India (0% pledge).
weaknesses: Sequential top-line interest revenue dipped -3.27% QoQ (₹97,814 Cr vs ₹1,01,126 Cr in Q4 FY26) due to seasonal Q1 fee moderation.
Deposit growth (+8.2% YoY) trails credit growth (+15.4% YoY), elevating the Credit-to-Deposit (CD) ratio toward 76.5%.
High operating expenses from wage revision provisions and pension liabilities compared to private-sector banking peers.
opportunities: Monetization of 80M+ registered users on the YONO digital banking platform for cross-selling insurance, mutual funds, and pre-approved loans.
Strong corporate capex pipeline in infrastructure, renewable energy, and manufacturing driving high-rated wholesale credit demand.
Potential stake unlocking and dividend upstreaming from high-growth subsidiaries (SBI Life, SBI Cards, SBI Mutual Fund).
threats: Expected RBI repo rate cuts in upcoming quarters could compress floating-rate loan yields before term deposits reprice downward.
System-wide competition for retail term deposits forcing higher cost of funds across Indian public and private banks.
Macroeconomic or monsoon shocks potentially impacting agricultural and unsecured retail Xpress Credit delinquencies.
